claims.claim: Exact certificate characterization: G contains K6 minus an edge as an induced minor exactly when it has six pairwise-disjoint nonempty connected vertex sets A,B,C1,C2,C3,C4 such that A and B are anticomplete and every other pair of sets has an edge between it. Consequently detection is in NP and has an O(7^n n²) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: Under vertex deletions and edge contractions, the inverse image of every surviving target vertex is a disjoint nonempty connected branch set. Two quotient vertices are adjacent exactly when an edge joins their branch sets, so the sole target nonedge is precisely A-B anticompleteness. Conversely, delete unused vertices and contract a spanning tree in each set. Seven labels enumerate every possible model; all conditions are testable in O(n²), and the labeling is a polynomial-size NP certificate.
claims.search_method: Proved both directions directly from induced-minor operations and checked that the enumeration enforces disjointness, connectivity, all fourteen required adjacencies, and the unique forbidden adjacency.

claims.claim: Let q be the number of nonedges of G. Detection is fixed-parameter tractable in q, in time O(7^(2q+3)n²), and undecided instances have at most 2q+3 vertices. In particular, the problem is polynomial-time solvable when q=O(log n).
claims.evidence: A clique has no two nonempty anticomplete sets. If q>0 and four universal vertices exist, the endpoints of any nonedge plus those four vertices induce K6 minus that edge. Otherwise at most three vertices are universal, while every nonuniversal vertex is an endpoint of one of the q nonedges; hence n≤2q+3. Applying claim 0 gives the stated FPT bound. When q≤C log n for a fixed C, the exponential factor is polynomial in n.
claims.search_method: Direct endpoint counting and verification of the universal-vertex construction, supplemented by exhaustive enumeration of every labeled graph through six vertices.

claims.claim: On chordal graphs, K6 minus an edge is an induced minor if and only if it is already an induced subgraph. Thus chordal inputs can be decided in O(n^6) time by enumerating six vertices. The same argument works for Kt minus an edge for every fixed t≥3.
claims.evidence: Restrict to the branch sets. The t−2 core sets yield internally disjoint A-B paths, so an inclusion-minimal A-B separator S has size at least t−2. In a chordal graph every such minimal separator is a clique. Each full component D of G−S contains an S-complete vertex: maximize |N(v)∩S| in D; if v misses s∈S, a shortest path from v to a neighbor of s and chordality force its last vertex to retain every S-neighbor of v and additionally see s, a contradiction. S-complete vertices in the A- and B-components are nonadjacent; together with any t−2 vertices of S they induce Kt minus an edge. The reverse implication is immediate, and enumeration costs O(n^t), hence O(n^6) for t=6.
claims.search_method: Completed the minimal-separator proof and exhaustively searched all labeled graphs on t+1 vertices for t=3,4,5,6; among 636,712 chordal graphs, no one-extra-vertex contraction model lacked the asserted induced subgraph.

claims.claim: There is an explicit polynomial-time classification on complete multipartite graphs. Let the part sizes be n1,…,nr. For every i with ni≥2, reserve two vertices of part i and put mi=ni−2 and mj=nj for j≠i. Accept exactly when, for some s∈{0,…,4} and some s distinct indices J⊆{1,…,r}\{i}, subtracting one from each mj with j∈J leaves counts whose complete multipartite graph has a matching of size at least 4−s. If the residual total is M and its largest part has size L, this matching size is min(⌊M/2⌋,M−L).
claims.evidence: Anticompleteness forces both exceptional sets into one part, and connectivity then forces both to be singletons. Every core is either a singleton in a distinct outside part or intersects at least two parts and can be shrunk to one cross-part edge. Such edge-cores are automatically adjacent to every other edge-core and every outside-part singleton, so the remaining choice is exactly a matching after reserving the stated vertices. Any matching has size at most ⌊M/2⌋ and M−L; pairing across largest remaining parts attains their minimum. Enumerating i and at most four singleton parts is polynomial.
claims.search_method: Proved the branch-set normal form and matching formula, then compared the criterion against definition-level exhaustive branch-set search on all 138 complete-multipartite isomorphism types through ten vertices.

claims.claim: Given a tree decomposition of width w, detection is decidable in n·2^{O(w log w)} time; hence it is polynomial-time solvable on every fixed-width class supplied with such decompositions.
claims.evidence: A nice-decomposition DP can store seven-way bag labels, a connectivity partition refining those labels, unseen/active/closed status for each of the six labels, and fourteen required-adjacency bits, while rejecting every A-B edge. Forgetting the final representative of one component is legal only when it is the label's sole component, after which the label closes; separator locality proves it cannot reconnect later. Join states combine partitions by transitive closure and OR adjacency bits, rejecting two separately closed copies. Root acceptance is equivalent to six nonempty connected branch sets with exactly the required adjacency pattern. There are at most 7^(w+1)·Bell(w+1) times a constant number of states, and even quadratic join processing remains 2^{O(w log w)} per bag.
claims.search_method: Constructed and checked a full state invariant for introduce, edge, forget, join, and root operations, including the otherwise error-prone closed-component cases and state-count bound.

claims.claim: A model cannot in general be normalized so that either endpoint of the missing edge has a singleton branch set. A 12-vertex counterexample consists of anticomplete paths A=a1a2a3a4 and B=b1b2b3b4, a clique C={c1,c2,c3,c4}, and exactly the additional edges aici and bici for i=1,…,4.
claims.evidence: The two four-vertex paths and the four singleton ci sets form the displayed model. A singleton exceptional set needs four distinct neighbors, so it must be some ci. Its anticomplete opposite set is an interval in a component of A−ai or B−bi. Exact boundary enumeration leaves only eight intervals with four external neighbors. In every such case the four cores must use all four boundary vertices separately, including the endpoint ai adjacent only to the deleted singleton and the opposite interval. That endpoint is therefore an isolated singleton core and cannot meet the other three cores, a contradiction. The exact search exhaustively confirmed all cases.
claims.witness: A={a1,a2,a3,a4}, B={b1,b2,b3,b4}, and core sets {c1},{c2},{c3},{c4}; exhaustive search found no model with either exceptional branch set singleton.
claims.search_method: Combined the degree and interval-boundary proof with an exact integer-bit-mask search over 1,676 connected subsets and 1,264 ordered singleton/opposite-exception candidates; all eight candidates having boundary size four were rejected exhaustively.

target_evidence: The exact target requests an unrestricted complexity classification and, if tractable, a polynomial-time algorithm. The draft does not establish either a general polynomial-time algorithm or hardness/NP-completeness; it expressly says that unrestricted classification remains unresolved. Its exact certificate algorithm, dense-graph parameterization, chordal and multipartite classifications, bounded-treewidth algorithm, and normalization obstruction are nevertheless correct and material partial progress. Thus FULLY_RESOLVES_TARGET would be unjustified, while the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL and its restrained final writeup are accurate rather than overstated or understated.
checks_performed: Read only the authorized source input and revision draft; used no web, retrieval database, receipt, prior run, verification report, or other solution.
Reconstructed all six arguments from the definitions and checked target coverage independently of claimed_resolution and self_assessment.

Ran independent_exact_checks.py using integer bit masks only: all 138 complete-multipartite types through ten vertices matched the classification, all 33,867 labeled graphs through six vertices satisfied the dense preprocessing assertions, and the 12-vertex singleton-exception search was exhaustive.
Compiled and ran chordal_exact_checker.cpp: it checked 2,131,008 labeled graphs and all 636,712 chordal instances in the one-extra-vertex cases for t=3 through 6 without finding a discrepancy.
Used no floating-point arithmetic in any decision; both checker sources are persisted under the required audit directory.
